chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from his brother al-Hasan said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man dies and he has no heir except his mawali (freedmen/clients) who emancipated him. Do they inherit him? And whose is his inheritance? He (peace be upon him) wrote back: 'For his highest mawla.'

key_terms.مَوَالِيهِ: Mawali (freedmen or clients who have a patronage relationship with the freed person)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits a person if they have no heirs except the mawali who freed them?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Jawad (or al-Baqir, depending on the specific chain interpretation in Tusi's compilation) clarifies that when a freed slave dies without other heirs, his inheritance passes to his *mawla* (patron), specifically the 'highest' or most senior one among them. This ruling underscores the legal bond of *wilayah* established through manumission, treating the patron as a residual heir (*asabah*) in the absence of agnatic relatives, a key principle in Shia inheritance jurisprudence.
